title: resilience-testing-pack
description: Structured second-line resilience-testing pack record for an important business service or a critical-or-important third-party arrangement at a regulated financial institution. Carries the subject of test, the mapping summary, the impact tolerance under test, the severe-but-plausible scenario set, the test-design choices per scenario (method, cadence, preconditions, safety controls, exit triggers), the success criteria tied to tolerance, the evidence-collection and observation plan, the read-out template the operational-resilience committee receives, the lessons-learned-and-findings flow into issue management, and the integration into the firm's annual testing programme. Consumes vendor-diligence (criticality, subcontractors, data_access), exit-plan (testing_plan and exit-rehearsal scenarios), and the firm's IBS map (impact tolerance). Downstream consumers: dora-register-builder for ICT-third-party register entries where DORA applies; issue-writeup for findings flow.

pack_id.description: Stable identifier for this testing pack. Carried into the read-out, the lessons-learned record, and the next-cycle plan.

engagement_id.description: Optional pointer to the scope record under which this pack was produced.

as_of_date.description: Date the pack was last revised.

subject_type.description: Whether the test subject is an important business service end-to-end, a single third-party arrangement, or a portfolio cut (e.g., the firm's hyperscaler-region exposure across multiple arrangements).

subject_id.description: Stable identifier for the IBS, arrangement, or portfolio under test. Reused across the IBS map, vendor-diligence, exit-plan, and the dora register where applicable.

subject_description.description: Plain-language description of what is under test (e.g., 'card-payment authorisation IBS', 'foundation-model API supporting AML investigator narrative summarisation', 'hyperscaler primary-region exposure for the customer-onboarding chain').

review_type.description: Why this pack is being produced. Drives depth, scenario set, and review-gate set.

dora_in_scope.description: True when the firm or the function is in scope for DORA digital operational resilience testing programme expectations.

tlpt_in_scope.description: True when the firm is designated for advanced testing including threat-led penetration testing under the relevant supervisory framework. TLPT scoping requires legal and supervisory engagement and sits outside the operational tabletop / simulation set.

ai_in_scope.description: True when an AI vendor or AI-driven function sits on the chain under test. Surfaces AI-specific scenarios (model regression, eval drift, prompt-injection on the deployed system, vendor model deprecation mid-cycle, training-data incident at the vendor).

mapping_summary.description: Snapshot of the IBS or arrangement mapping under test. The pack consumes; it does not re-do mapping.

process_chain.description: Plain-language description of the process chain end-to-end.

fourth_parties.description: Material fourth parties (hyperscaler regions, BIN-sponsor processors, KYC vendors, fund-accountant subcontractors, foundation-model upstreams).

internal_dependencies.description: Internal systems, data stores, and control points on the chain.

impact_tolerance.description: The firm-defined tolerance the test is calibrated against. Sourced from the firm's IBS map. Vendor SLAs are not the test.

source.description: Where the tolerance comes from (firm IBS map, board-approved tolerance statement, regulatory submission).

customer_impact_threshold.description: Customer-impact ceiling (e.g., 'no more than X percent of authorisation requests declined for connectivity reasons over the disruption window').

regulatory_impact_threshold.description: Threshold above which the disruption is supervisorily reportable.

financial_impact_threshold.description: Loss-or-cost ceiling tied to risk-appetite where applicable.

scenarios.description: Severe-but-plausible scenarios under test. Each scenario is grounded in a public-source plausibility anchor (a real prior event of the same shape, a regulator-cited scenario, an industry tabletop pack). 'Low likelihood' is not a basis for exclusion; severe-but-plausible is the supervisory frame.

rationale.description: Why this scenario was selected for this cycle (recent incident, supervisory direction, prior-test finding, concentration-risk-review output, exit-plan-driven rehearsal).

plausibility_anchor.description: Public-source anchor for the scenario (named prior incident in another firm, a regulator-cited scenario, a CISA tabletop pack reference). Cite by title and date in the source trace; do not name a non-defendant institution.

expected_stress.description: What the scenario is intended to stress (failover path, data integrity, operational decisioning under degraded telemetry, customer-communication readiness, supervisory-communication readiness).

severity.description: Designed severity of the scenario. Tolerance-breach scenarios are the test of recovery posture under failure of the primary path.

ai_specific.description: True when the scenario specifically tests an AI dependency (vendor model regression, eval drift on the deployed system, prompt-injection on the deployed agent, vendor model deprecation).

test_design.description: Per-scenario test method, cadence, preconditions, safety controls, and exit triggers. A programme that uses tabletop everywhere has not been tested in supervisory terms; a programme that runs full-live everywhere is reckless.

method.description: Test method. Methods escalate in fidelity and operational risk; mix the methods across the programme.

cadence.description: How often the test runs (one-off this cycle, annual, semi-annual, quarterly, multi-year for full-live).

preconditions.description: What must be true before the test runs (legal sign-off for live tests, vendor participation confirmed, customer-communication safety controls in place, kill-switch ready, regulator-observation posture set).

safety_controls.description: Controls that prevent a partial-simulation or live test from becoming a real incident (rollback procedure, customer-impact-threshold for early termination, data-integrity checkpoints, comms-suppression while in-test).

exit_triggers.description: Conditions that terminate the test before completion (real customer-impact threshold hit, real incident on an unrelated path, vendor declares an issue, supervisor intervention).

participants.description: Roles in the test: business operations, technology operations, vendor counterpart, second-line risk, internal audit observer, supervisor observer where applicable.

vendor_participation.description: Vendor's role in the test. 'None' on a critical-or-important arrangement is itself a finding. A test the vendor declines to join tests the partnership, not just the technology.

success_criteria.description: Per-scenario success criteria tied to the impact tolerance. Each criterion has a measurable threshold; a 'pass' that cannot be evidenced is not a pass.

metric.description: What is measured (recovery time, data integrity check success rate, customer-impact volume, decisioning latency, comms cycle time).

threshold.description: The success or fail line. Tied to the impact tolerance, not to the vendor's published SLA.

tolerance_link.description: Which line of the impact tolerance the criterion maps to.

evidence_collection_plan.description: What evidence is captured during the exercise, by whom, in what form, and how it is preserved for the read-out, the lessons-learned record, and any later supervisory inspection.

form.description: Logs, screenshots, recorded conversations, vendor-side ticket exports, system traces, observer notes.

retention.description: How long the evidence is retained and where. Supervisory inspection windows often run several years.

observation_method.description: How the exercise is observed (in-room observers per workstream, recorded video, command-and-control bridge transcript, after-action interviews). Independent observation is the second-line role; first-line runs the exercise.

communication_plan.description: Internal and external communication during and after the exercise.

customer_communication.description: Customer-facing communication where the test may surface real customer impact (full-live exercise, shadow-cutover on a customer-affecting path). Suppressed where the test is non-customer-affecting.

regulator_communication.description: Supervisor pre-notification, observation invitation, post-test read-out where applicable. Industry-wide tests and TLPT carry their own supervisory engagement model.

readout_template_sections.description: Named sections the operational-resilience committee receives in the post-exercise read-out. Locked at design time so the post-exercise narrative shape is not invented under time pressure.

findings_actions_framework.description: How findings flow from the exercise into the firm's issue-management cycle. References issue-writeup. Findings without owners and clocks die in the post-exercise deck.

lessons_learned_capture.description: How lessons are captured beyond findings (process improvements, runbook updates, training implications, programme-design adjustments). Filed against the IBS or arrangement, not against the test cycle, so the next cycle benefits.

post_test_remediation.description: Remediation actions arising from the exercise. Each carries an owner, a clock, and a verification path. A pack that does not produce remediation has not tested anything that mattered.

programme_alignment.description: How this pack sits inside the firm's annual testing programme and any regulator-mandated programme.

dora_programme_link.description: Where this pack sits in the digital operational resilience testing programme under DORA Article 24, where applicable.

reg_sci_link.description: Where this pack sits in the Reg SCI testing programme (industry-wide test, BCDR test, designated members) at SCI entities.

tlpt_link.description: Cross-reference to the TLPT exercise where the firm is in scope and the testing pack scenarios feed the TLPT.

exit_plan_record_id.description: Cross-reference to the exit-plan record where this pack contains an exit-rehearsal scenario.

vendor_diligence_record_ids.description: Cross-references to the vendor-diligence records for the third parties in scope.

concentration_risk_review_record_id.description: Cross-reference to a concentration-risk-review where a portfolio scenario in this pack tests a flagged concentration.

reviewer_questions.description: Questions for the human approver. Each names the decision it supports.

review_gates.description: Named human-review gates this pack must clear. Drawn from references/review-gates.md.

owner.description: Role accountable for the design and execution of the exercise. Usually the BCDR lead or the head of operational resilience for IBS-level packs; the head of TPRM for arrangement-level packs.

approver.description: Role of the human approver named in the firm's operational-resilience policy for tests of this scope and method.

next_cycle_trigger.description: When the next cycle of this scenario or pack is due. Annual cadence is the floor for critical-or-important arrangements; some scenarios run more often.

confidence_label.description: Confidence in the overall pack, per references/review-gates.md.

source_trace.description: Citations supporting material claims. Every claim should be traceable.
